name: Meta-Policy Reflexion (MPR)
venue: arXiv preprint (arXiv:2509.03990, cs.AI); not peer-reviewed as of writing
authors_affiliation: Chunlong Wu, Ye Luo, Zhibo Qu, Min Wang — Tongji University (corresponding: wuchunlong@tongji.edu.cn)
code_url: N/A (no public code repository released; the paper repeatedly refers to 'the provided implementation' and an 'uploaded spreadsheet' but supplies no GitHub/Zenodo link)
task_domain: Embodied / interactive text-based agent decision-making (household task completion). Single-agent sequential decision-making framed as an MDP.
problem_setting: Interactive, single-agent, text-based embodied environment (AlfWorld) modeled as an MDP M=(S,A,P,r,gamma). A frozen LLM (Qwen3-32b) acts as the base policy generating natural-language actions under deterministic/low-temperature decoding. Supervision is via environment success/failure signals (no ground-truth action labels, no model weight updates). The setting separates a training phase (memory is updated after failed episodes on a 60-task train set) from an inference phase (memory frozen, used to guide decoding plus hard admissibility, evaluated on a 74-task held-out test set). Goal: distill ephemeral per-episode reflections into reusable cross-task corrective knowledge without RL/fine-tuning.
what_is_retrieved: Structured, predicate-like corrective rules ('meta-policy' rules with confidence weights) distilled from hindsight reflections of past failed trajectories; stored in a Meta-Policy Memory (MPM). At each step a state-relevant subset of these rules is retrieved.
retrieval_grounding: GROWING / episodic agent-written memory. The Meta-Policy Memory (MPM) is built and grown online from the agent's own failed trajectories during the training phase, then frozen at inference. It is not a static external corpus (no docs/KB/API store).
completeness_vs_topk_objective: Precision/relevance-driven variable-size selection: at each step a state-relevant rule subset M_t ⊆ M is retrieved (no fixed top-k ranking objective stated; not a completeness-of-minimal-set objective). [uncertain] — the paper does not specify the exact selection size or scoring; relevance to current state is the stated criterion.
cbr_cycle_coverage: Retrieve (state-relevant rule subset), Reuse (soft memory-conditioned decoding), Retain (write distilled rules from failed episodes into MPM). Revise is partial: the LLM reflection function f(τ) generalizes/abstracts new rules, and HAC enforces constraints, but there is no explicit per-case adaptation/repair loop. Flags: [Retrieve: yes, Reuse: yes, Revise: partial, Retain: yes]
explicit_cbr_grounding: False. The work does NOT frame itself as case-based reasoning and does not cite Aamodt & Plaza or Kolodner; it is positioned as reflective memory / verbal-RL extension (Reflexion lineage). It realizes CBR-like retain-and-reuse mechanisms under the 'meta-policy memory' framing rather than CBR terminology.
retrieval_unit: guideline-rule: a predicate-like, generalized corrective rule (with confidence weight) distilled from a failed trajectory's reflection. Not a raw trajectory or single demo — an abstracted rule.
index_source: Growing memory, online/test-time-induced (during training rounds). MPM is initialized empty (M ← ∅) and accumulates rules via M ← M ∪ f(τ) after failed episodes; it is frozen for the inference/evaluation phase. Construction is online during the training phase, then static at deployment.
index_structure_topology: Flat set/collection of predicate-like rules with confidence weights (M is a set; updates are set-union). No graph or hierarchical index is implemented; the paper proposes graph-based/distributed memory only as future work. [uncertain] — exact internal indexing (e.g., embedding vs. keyword keying for state-relevant retrieval) is not detailed.
retriever_type: LLM-mediated / context-level selection: a state-relevant subset M_t is selected and injected into the prompt; retrieval operates entirely at the prompt level with no logit modification. The paper does not specify a dense/BM25 retriever — selection of state-relevant rules appears LLM/context-driven. [uncertain] on exact retriever implementation.
retriever_learning_signal: None (no trained retriever). Rule extraction is driven by environment success/failure (failed episodes trigger LLM reflection f(τ)); rules carry confidence weights, but rule selection/retrieval itself is not a learned/optimized retriever — it is off-the-shelf state-relevance matching. The improvement signal is downstream-task failure feedback used to grow memory, not to train a retriever.
query_construction: The query/key is the current environment state s_t; a state-relevant rule subset M_t is retrieved and the LLM conditions on (s_t, M_t). No decomposed sub-queries or synthetic query expansion described.
query_granularity: Step/state-level: retrieval of the relevant rule subset M_t occurs at each step t conditioned on the current state s_t.
when_to_retrieve: Iterative / per-step: at every decision step the agent retrieves a state-relevant rule subset before generating the action.
retrieval_trigger_signal: Fixed schedule (per-step, every step): retrieval of M_t happens at each step conditioned on s_t. There is no uncertainty- or confidence-triggered gating; memory WRITE (not retrieval) is triggered by episode failure.
reranking: None. No reranking stage is described; a state-relevant subset is selected and injected directly.
retrieved_context_refinement: None explicit beyond selecting the state-relevant subset. Rules are distilled/abstracted at write time (via LLM reflection), not refined post-retrieval; no compression/decompose/distractor-filtering stage at retrieval time is described.
tool_document_engineering: N/A (no tool/skill descriptions are indexed; retrieved units are corrective rules, not tools).
index_content_separation: N/A — no separation of a lightweight index from heavy on-demand content; MPM stores compact predicate-like rules directly.
dynamic_index_and_protocol: N/A (no external tool index or integration protocol such as RapidAPI/MCP/function-calling).
how_retrieved_used: Two complementary mechanisms: (1) SOFT prompt augmentation — memory-conditioned decoding where the retrieved rule subset M_t is injected into the LLM prompt to bias decoding toward memory-supported actions, a_t = π_θ(s_t, M_t), with no logit/weight changes; (2) HARD rule admissibility check (HAC) — the generated action a_t is validated post-hoc against a constraint set C(s_t); if a_t ∉ C(s_t) the agent resamples with adjusted memory/context or falls back to a safe action.
planning_integration: Per-step interleaved retrieval-augmented acting: at each step the agent retrieves state-relevant rules, conditions decoding on them (soft guidance), generates an action, then applies hard admissibility filtering before executing in the environment. No tree search/MCTS; it is a retrieve-then-act loop within an MDP rollout, with offline memory growth between episodes.
reasoning_search_interleaving_granularit: Per-tool-call / per-action-step within a rollout: retrieval and admissibility checking occur at each environment action step.
adaptation_mechanism: LLM-prompted soft adaptation plus post-hoc constraint validation: retrieved rules bias the frozen LLM's decoding (verbatim-rule-in-prompt soft guidance), and HAC enforces hard constraints with resample/safe-fallback. New rules are produced by execution-feedback-driven (failure-triggered) LLM reflection f(τ), not by per-case revision of a retrieved case.
retrieved_item_representation: Distilled strategy/guideline injected as structured, predicate-like text rules (with confidence weights) into the prompt. Not raw trajectories, not executable programs, not latent tokens.
abstraction_level_of_retrieved_unit: State-aware guideline/rule (distilled, generalized corrective rule), more abstract than a raw trajectory or single demonstration; predicate-like form derived from failure analysis.
noise_robustness_mechanism: Hard rule admissibility check (HAC): post-generation validation of actions against an environment/user constraint set C(s_t), with resample or safe-fallback for inadmissible actions — guards against invalid/unsafe actions. Confidence weights on rules and the predicate-like format aim to improve quality/interpretability, but the paper notes LLM-generated rules may contain redundancies/inconsistencies (no learned relevance evaluator or distractor-aware training).
memory_type: episodic-derived structured rule memory (Meta-Policy Memory, MPM): an external, predicate-like rule store distilled from episodic failures; closest to a guideline/rule library rather than a skill-library, graph, or latent memory.
write_back: True. The system writes distilled corrective rules into MPM after failed episodes: M ← M ∪ f(τ), where f is an LLM reflection function over a failed trajectory τ.
online_growth: Partial / phase-dependent: the store grows online during the training phase (rounds where meta-policy update is enabled) but is FROZEN at inference/test time (no memory update on the held-out test set). So it grows during training-time interaction, not during deployment evaluation.
write_back_trigger: On-failure only (reflective): a write occurs only when an episode fails, after which the LLM reflects on the failure and extracts corrective rules. Successful episodes do not trigger writes.
failure_experience_usage: Failure-only corrective rules: only failed trajectories are reflected upon to extract corrective predicate-like rules; there is no success-based or success+failure contrastive storage.
memory_evolution_update: Append-only (set union M ← M ∪ f(τ)). No dedup-merge, delta-update, refine-overwrite, or pruning is implemented; the paper lists automatic rule management (confidence weighting, redundancy detection, abstraction, pruning) only as future work.
retrieval_as_learned_policy: No. Retrieval/rule-selection is not a learned or RL-optimized policy; it is state-relevance-based selection over the rule set. The base LLM policy is frozen and not fine-tuned. MPR explicitly contrasts itself with RL approaches that require parameter updates.
cross_agent_or_cross_framework_sharing: No — single-agent private memory. Multi-agent / graph-based shared-and-negotiated rule memory is proposed only as future work.
benchmarks: AlfWorld (text-based embodied agent environment). Train set: 60 tasks; held-out test set: 74 tasks.
baselines: Reflexion (verbal reinforcement learning / textual self-reflection). ReAct is discussed as related background but the quantitative comparison is against Reflexion. Ablation-style internal comparison: MPR vs. MPR+HAC.
key_metrics: Execution accuracy (% of tasks completed correctly), reported per training round (Rounds 1-5) and as a sixth-round held-out comparison.
headline_result: On the 74-task held-out test set: MPR+HAC reaches 91.4% accuracy vs. Reflexion 86.9% (6 reflection rounds on test set) and MPR-without-HAC 87.8% (trained 5 rounds on train set, single evaluation). On the 60-task training set MPR reaches 100% by Round 3 vs. Reflexion's 88.3% by Round 5.
ablations: HAC ablation is the central one: MPR (memory-conditioned decoding only) = 87.8% vs. MPR + HAC (hard admissibility at test time) = 91.4% on the 74-task test set, isolating the +3.6-point contribution of hard admissibility checks on top of soft memory-guided decoding. Per-round training-set curve (Reflexion 70.0->88.3 over Rounds 1-5 vs. MPR 83.9->100.0, reaching 100% by Round 3) isolates the value of consolidated reusable rules vs. ephemeral reflection. No retriever/rule-selection ablation reported.
evaluation_decoupling: No. Only end-to-end task execution accuracy is reported; no intrinsic retrieval metrics (Recall@k / nDCG / rule-selection precision) are reported separately.
process_vs_outcome_metrics: Outcome-only: evaluation scores final task execution accuracy; no intermediate process-quality metrics (reasoning faithfulness, step-wise retrieval accuracy, trajectory quality) are quantified. The paper recommends per-task inspection but does not report process metrics.
cost_efficiency_tradeoff: Framed as resource-efficient: no model weight updates / no RL fine-tuning (the LLM stays frozen), positioned against RL alternatives that need substantial compute. Cross-task transfer reduces per-task reflection cost — MPR needs only a single test-set evaluation pass (after 5 train-set rounds) to beat Reflexion's 6 in-situ reflection rounds. No concrete token-count, latency, or API-cost numbers are reported. [uncertain] on quantitative cost figures.
context_budget_and_selection_count: A state-relevant rule subset M_t ⊆ M is injected per step via prompt-level conditioning; exact k / token budget for the injected rule subset is not specified. [uncertain] — no fixed-k or budget cap is reported.
survey_scope_and_axes: N/A (this is a method paper, not a survey/benchmark).
benchmark_construction_and_size: N/A (uses existing AlfWorld; not a benchmark-construction paper). For reference: 60 train tasks + 74 test tasks; best reported system MPR+HAC = 91.4% on the 74-task test set.
builds_on: Reflexion (Shinn et al., 2023, verbal reinforcement learning / textual self-reflection) as the primary predecessor; ReAct (Yao et al., 2022/2023, reasoning+acting interleaving); AlfWorld (Shridhar et al., 2020) as the environment. Related memory work cited: A-Mem, G-Memory, Memory-R1, SAGE, and Zhang et al.'s memory-mechanism survey.
contrasts_with: Reflexion / ReAct (ephemeral, task-specific reflective traces not reused across tasks) and RL / RLHF policy-adaptation methods (transferable but requiring substantial parameter updates and compute). MPR positions itself as keeping the lightweight flexibility of textual reflection while distilling reusable, structured, transferable rules without weight updates.
lineage: Group D — case-based / experience-based planning (reflective experiential memory for agents). Sits in the reflective-memory lineage extending Reflexion toward persistent, cross-task reusable corrective rules plus hard admissibility constraints; CBR-like Retain/Reuse realized without explicit CBR framing.
